newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dlr sinks on overseas selling, holed by aussie.
newsitem.headline: NZ dlr sinks on overseas selling, holed by aussie.

text.p: Foreign traders, scenting another easing in New Zealand monetary policy on the horizon, sold the kiwi on Thursday and by the close it was at its day's lows against the U.S. dollar, with the sickly Australian unit contributing to its neighbour's woes.

"There is a slightly weaker bias feeding in and we've seen a good bit of volume go through today," a senior Wellington dealer said. By the close the dollar stood at 0.6713/20 to the U.S. unit and some traders saw 67 cents being challenged overnight.
"There has been genuine selling -- it's American and it's been matched to an extent by local buying and short-covering -- it's certainly not local selling," another said.

Players here, while aware that upcoming indicators are unlikely to suggest that monetary policy should be tightened, remain concerned that the Reserve Bank's Monetary Conditions Index (MCI) is pushing at the limits of the RB's tolerance.
"The bias is for an easing, but people here aren't keen to shove on the MCI too much," the trader said.

While sentiment remained edgy, and was not helped by the weakness in the Australian dollar after jobs data there again suggested another rate cut might be on the way, traders thought it might be tough for the kiwi to go below 67 cents.
"Assuming the (U.S.) dollar holds relative, I don't think it will go to much lower -- maybe through 67 but we're more likely to see a 0.6705-25 range short-term," one added.
The trade-weighted index (TWI) remained stranded below 66 at 65.97 by the close, close to its opening level of 65.99.
